content.text: The text discusses historical treatment of diabetes, emphasizing milk or skim-milk diets, peptonized milk, low-carbohydrate foods, selected vegetables, gluten/bran/almond substitutes, hygiene, mineral waters, and drugs such as codeine and ergot. It then describes scrofula as an inherited or acquired constitutional tendency causing chronic lymphatic, skin, bone, and joint inflammation, associated with poor nutrition, overcrowding, and inadequate ventilation; prevention and treatment stress breastfeeding, animal food, fresh air, bathing, iodine, cod-liver oil, and constitutional care. A lengthy section on hereditary syphilis covers transmission by either parent, pregnancy risks, congenital symptoms, bone, liver, spleen, eye, ear, dental, and nervous lesions, diagnosis, prognosis, and mercury-based treatment. Finally, stomatitis—including catarrhal, aphthous, thrush, ulcerative, and gangrenous forms—is reviewed, with emphasis on hygiene, nutrition, oral cleansing, and topical remedies. Milk for peptonization is warmed in a pitcher of hot water or a warm place.
